objective: Reduce median-of-repetition mean request latency while preserving the complete notes API contract and durability.

plan.change: def create_note(title: str, body: str, tags: list[str]) -> Note:    connection = _connect()    payload = _normalize_tags(tags)    cursor = connection.execute(        'INSERT INTO notes (title, body, tags) VALUES (?, ?, ?)',        (title, body, payload),    )    note_id = cursor.lastrowid    connection.commit()    row = connection.execute(        'SELECT id, title, body, tags FROM notes WHERE id = ?',        (note_id,),    ).fetchone()    _release(connection)    return _to_note(row)
plan.hypothesis: The current create_note implementation performs an INSERT followed by a full table scan (SELECT * FROM notes) to find the newly created note by ID. This results in O(N) database reads and O(N) Python object construction/validation for every creation, regardless of the total number of notes. By changing the retrieval query to filter by the specific ID returned by lastrowid (WHERE id = ?), we reduce the database work to a single row lookup (O(1) with primary key index) and eliminate the overhead of constructing Note objects for all other rows. This should significantly reduce latency for create_note, which is a frequent operation.
risks: The optimization is isolated to create_note; other operations like list_notes still have inefficiencies.
The improvement is measured in a controlled environment; production performance may vary with higher concurrency or larger datasets.
The patch does not address similar inefficiencies in update_note or delete_note which have already been optimized in prior iterations.
